Felix! Yes, obviously. The sofa is yours 15 to 19 May and Niamh says she'll hide the good coffee from you this time.

Send me your flight when you have it. Do you still not eat anything with coriander or did Lotte cure you of that?

L

Dear Luis,

It is late and the radiator under my desk is ticking like a metronome, which is the only reason I am still awake to answer you. Lotte has discovered that the bottom drawer of the plan chest opens, and that it is full of paper, so the studio now looks like a ticker-tape parade.

Thank you for the sofa. I booked the flights tonight: I land at Stansted on Thursday 15 May at 18:55 and fly home on Monday 19 May at 14:30, so I will be out of your hair by lunchtime. I will take the train in and then the overground, I think, so I should be at Albion Road around half past nine. The conference (Letterform Days, at the old granary building in King's Cross) is Friday and Saturday, and I give my little talk on Saturday at 11.

Coriander: still no. Lotte eats it by the handful and looks at me with pity.

One question. Is there anywhere near you that could print about twenty A3 sheets on good paper before I arrive? I want to hand out specimens at the conference and the German post office will crease them.

Love, Felix

9.30 Thursday works. Overground to Rectory Road is easiest.

Try Inkhouse on Stoke Newington Church Street for the A3s. If they deliver, it's Flat 3, 14 Albion Road, N16. I'll put them somewhere safe. We might have a cat by then.
L

Dear Luis,

The cat-to-be! I read all the way back to the top to see if I had missed an announcement. I want a name and a photograph.

I have written to Inkhouse and they will print twenty sheets on a warm uncoated stock and deliver them to you on Tuesday 13 May. So that is settled, and so am I.

Love, Felix

subject: Saturday dinner with the old desk lot?

messages.text:
Dear Luis,

It is Easter Saturday and Berlin has gone quiet in the way it only does on holidays, so I am at the kitchen table with a coffee and the window open, listening to a neighbour practise the same four bars of a trumpet piece over and over.

I have had an idea, and you are allowed to tell me it is a bad one. While I am in London, could we get the old MA studio together for dinner? Saturday 17 May, after my talk. I am thinking of Priyanka, Tom W, Hana, Josef if he is still in Margate, and of course Niamh. Somewhere cheap and loud where nobody minds if we stay until they put the chairs on the tables.

I do not know who still lives in London, and you do, so this is me handing you a job and pretending it is a gift.

Love, Felix

Not a bad idea. I've written to everyone. Priyanka's in, Hana's in, Tom W is "probably" which means no. Josef is in Lisbon now apparently.

I've booked Bao Tan on Kingsland Road, Saturday 17 May, 8pm, table for 7, booking ref BT-4471. Cheap, loud, they never rush you.

Dear Luis,

Small disaster, though only a small one. The conference has moved my talk from Saturday morning to Saturday at 17:30, the last slot of the day, because the keynote speaker's flight changed. Then there is a reception after, which I am told I cannot escape because I am one of the people being received.

So I would not get to Kingsland Road before ten, and I would be the kind of tired where I only nod. I am sorry. I know you did the work.

Could we move it? Or, if not, cancel it and just have dinner at yours on the Friday, the three of us? I would honestly like that more.

Love, Felix

Friday at ours it is. Hana and Priyanka can't do any other night that week so I've cancelled the table at Bao Tan and told them. They send love and want photos of Lotte.

Niamh's making the dal. No coriander, I've already been told twice.

Tell Niamh I’ll bring wine.

Love, Felix

subject: A lens in want of a good home

messages.text:
Dear all,

Forgive a message that has nothing to do with books.  I have been clearing the box room before my daughter descends at New Year, and I find I own a camera I have not used since the Blair government and a lens that deserves better than a drawer.

The lens is a 50mm f/1.4 for the old K mount, bought new in 1984 in a shop on the Lothian Road that is now, inevitably, a coffee chain.  It has been in a leather case for most of its life.  The glass is clear as far as my eyes can tell, which, I grant you, is not very far.  The camera body I shall give to the charity shop; the lens I would rather sell to someone who will use it.  I had in mind ninety pounds, though I am open to persuasion, particularly by someone who has finished the Trollope.

I seem to remember Luis carrying a camera to the summer picnic, hence this round robin, but any of you is welcome to it.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

I'd love it. I've got a K-mount adapter already. Does the aperture ring still click? Any haze if you shine a torch through it?

I am still on the same page of Trollope.
L

Dear Luis,

I have done as you asked, with a bicycle lamp, in the airing cupboard, which my neighbour across the road must have found an interesting spectacle.

The aperture ring clicks at every stop from 1.4 to 22, firmly, like a well-made gate.  There is no haze that I can see.  There is a single speck of dust inside, near the edge, of the size one would describe in a school report as "hardly worth mentioning".  The focus ring is smooth, perhaps a shade stiff when cold, but then so am I.

As you have not finished the Trollope, the price is ninety pounds.  Had you finished it, it would have been eighty.  I am a man of principle.

I am at home most days.  Highbury is not far from you, I think?

Yours, Hamish Fairweather
£90 works. Friday 19th at 6.30? We fly to Cork on Saturday. Cash or transfer?

Dear Luis,

Friday at half past six suits me admirably.  The address is 9 Aberdour Road, N5, the house with the blue door and the unpruned rose, which I am told is an eyesore.  Ring twice; the bell is unreliable and so is my hearing.

Cash, please.  I have never transferred anything to anyone by telephone and I do not intend to begin at seventy.

I shall have the lens cleaned, boxed and ready, with its caps and the original receipt, which I found folded inside the case and which may amuse you.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

Hamish, thank you again. It's on the camera already and it's beautiful. First test shot is Biscuit asleep on a suitcase, which I'll print and bring to book club in January.

The receipt is great. £139 in 1984!

Merry Christmas,
Luis

Dear Luis,

I am glad it has gone to a good home and a better photographer.  Safe travels to Cork, and a happy Christmas to you both.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

truth.summary: Luis bought Hamish's 50mm f/1.4 K-mount lens for £90 cash, collecting it at Hamish's house on Friday 19 December 2025 before flying to Cork.

subject: Young Makers: a mentoring session with one of your designers?

messages.text:
Dear Luis,

A request slightly outside the relaunch, which I hope you will not mind.

1. The museum runs a Young Makers traineeship each summer. This year our digital trainee, Sade, is nineteen, self-taught, and very keen on interface design.
2. Part of the traineeship is one mentoring session with a working professional. Would someone at Acme be willing to give her an hour in July, ideally at the museum?
3. I attach Sade's portfolio, which she put together herself. She knows it has gaps and would welcome being told where.
4. There is no fee, I am afraid, but there is cake, and our gratitude is genuine.

I understand completely if July is too busy with the copy migration.

With best wishes,
Margaret Okafor
Head of Digital
Holloway Museum of Making | 30 Seven Sisters Road, London N7
Please direct collection enquiries to collections@hollowaymuseum.example.

Hi Margaret,

I've copied Jae. I think he'd be a good fit for Sade, and I'd like to sit in for the first half if I can.

Jae, could you look at the portfolio Margaret attached and let us know if July works?

Thanks,
Luis

Luis Cordero
Lead Product Designer, Acme Studio
3rd floor, 48 Turnmill Street, London EC1M 5RR
acme.example

Margaret, yes, happy to. Her bus timetable redesign is the strongest thing in there.
Only catch: Kestrel has a review on 2 July, so any time after that.

Jae

Dear Luis, dear Jae,

Thank you both, Sade was delighted. Three possible slots, all at the museum (staff entrance on Hornsey Road, ask for me at the desk):

1. Tuesday 7 July, 14:00 to 15:00
2. Thursday 9 July, 10:00 to 11:00
3. Monday 13 July, 15:30 to 16:30

Could you let me know which suits? I also attach our volunteer and visitor safeguarding form, which anyone meeting a trainee under the programme has to sign. One per person, please, returned before the day.

With best wishes,
Margaret Okafor
Head of Digital
Holloway Museum of Making | 30 Seven Sisters Road, London N7
Please direct collection enquiries to collections@hollowaymuseum.example.

All three work. Pick whichever you can make. I’ll do the form tonight.

Jae

Hello neighbours,

Three things, sorry. My mum is moving into Flat 1 at the start of August and she's just had a hip done, so:

1) does anyone know a good physio round here?
2) does anyone know a man with a van for a small move from Walthamstow, one bed and some boxes?
3) totally unrelated, my son Rory is resitting GCSE English in November and could do with a tutor. Not an agency, someone kind.

Thank you all so much.
Dot (Flat 6)

Hi Dot, we moved out of Flat 3 last month but I'm still on here, so:

1) Harriet Lowe at Dalston Step Clinic, fixed my shins last year. cc'd.
2) Tom (cc'd) sorted the van for our move, he'll know.
3) Hamish (cc'd) is a retired English teacher from my book club and the kindest person I know.

Hope your mum settles in well.
Luis

Hi Dot,

Thanks Luis. Happy to see your mum, but one thing up front: I don't do home visits, the clinic's on the ground floor and step-free though. If she's under six weeks post-op her hospital team should be seeing her first. Give the clinic a ring on 020 7946 0815 and ask for me.

Harriet
Harriet Lowe MCSP
Dalston Step Clinic, Dalston

Thank you Luis and Harriet! Tom, what do you charge for a half day with the van? Would a Saturday be ok?

ha no van here mate that was tariq i just carried a sofa badly  luis can you send dot his number
My mistake, Dot. I’ll send you Tariq’s number off-list.

Luis has been far too generous, but I should be very glad to meet Rory.  I no longer tutor for money; I do it for the pleasure of watching a young person discover that Mr Priestley is on their side.  Tuesday or Thursday afternoons suit me, in Highbury or at your kitchen table, whichever Rory finds less alarming.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

subject: Father of the bride, second draft: A or B?

messages.text:
Dear all,

I am writing to four people whose judgement I trust and who have the great advantage of never having met my daughter, so cannot take sides.  Some of you know each other, I believe, which is a small world and a smaller London.

Kirsty’s wedding is on the 28th of November in Edinburgh.  On Saturday Luis got my speech down from eleven minutes to seven.  I am stuck on how to begin it, and I should be grateful for a one-word answer, A or B.

A.  I open with the day Kirsty, aged nine, caught a trout on Loch Tay and insisted on putting it back, then cried because it swam off without thanking her.

B.  I open with four lines of Burns, which is expected at an Edinburgh wedding and which the groom's family, being from Surrey, will assume is profound.

The rest of the speech is the same either way.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

Hi Hamish,

A, without a doubt. Nobody remembers the Burns, everyone remembers the trout.

And hello Luis! Small world indeed. Hamish taught me A-level English in 1999 and I still can't use a semicolon without hearing him.

Best, Imogen

A. That bit made me laugh on Saturday.

Hi Imogen!
L

Hi Hamish,

A. And one tip from someone who speaks to rooms of runners: read it out loud standing up, twice, and wherever you run out of breath, that sentence is too long.

Harriet
Harriet Lowe MCSP
Dalston Step Clinic, Dalston

Hiya Hamish,

Still thinking about your Trollope rant from book club. A for me. You could tuck one line of Burns in right at the toast, to give the Surrey lot their profundity after all.

Jo x

Hiya Luis,

Still on for dinner on the 14th, yes? Ben keeps going out to the hall to take calls about it. I said I'd book somewhere myself and he nearly took my phone off me. Has he said anything to you?

Jo x

Dear all,

A it is, unanimously, which has never before happened in any committee I have sat on.  The trout opens, and Joanna's idea is adopted: one line of Burns at the toast, and no more.  I have read it standing up, as Harriet advised, and cut two sentences that very nearly killed me.

Thank you, all four of you.  I shall report back from Edinburgh.

Yours, Hamish Fairweather

facts: Posada es una mezcla de Veracruz y Chiapas con notas de piloncillo y canela. Va en la bolsa kraft de 250 g con válvula.
La cotización de $14,500 MXN + IVA incluye la etiqueta, el cartel y los archivos. El 50% se paga de anticipo y el resto contra entrega.
Si entra el anticipo esa semana, Luis propone mandar bocetos el 27 de octubre, recibir cambios hasta el 2 y entregar finales el 5 de noviembre.
El impresor es Chuy, de Grafos Atemajac. Los carteles tamaño carta son para los mostradores de Chapultepec y Providencia.
Ernesto irá a Coatepec el jueves 22.
El saldo del rediseño es de $43,000 MXN + IVA y venció el 15 de octubre.
Las bolsas de Posada van aparte de las de la fajilla de la fundación.
